data.title: ADR-001: TypeScript on Node.js as the core runtime
body: # ADR-001: TypeScript on Node.js as the core runtime
- **Status:** accepted
- **Scope:** stack
## Context
kadence has to run through `npx kadence` without prior installation — a requirement from the PRD (section 7.1). The guardrail on CLI startup is 200 ms for 1000 tasks.
Measured on the development machine (Node v25.8.2):
| What | Time |
| Cold start of an empty Node process | **40 ms** |
| Budget left for all the CLI's work | **160 ms** |
40 ms is 20% of the budget, spent before the first line of our own code. This is the main constraint the rest of the stack decisions depend on.
## Alternatives considered
| Option | Pros | Cons |

| TypeScript + Node | `npx` works without installation; the largest audience of OSS contributors; types as an executable specification of events | 40 ms eaten by the runtime start; a build step is needed |
| Go | ~2 ms start; a single static binary; ideal for a CLI | No `npx` — Homebrew/scoop/a curl script needed for every platform, which kills the "try it in 30 seconds" scenario |
| Rust | Fastest; reliability through types | The same as Go, plus a higher barrier to entry for contributors to an OSS project |
| Deno / Bun | Faster start than Node | A narrower audience; `npx` is still the dominant habit |
## Decision

**TypeScript, built to ESM, targeting Node 20+.** The minimum version is 20 LTS, not the current 25: demanding a fresh Node from a user who just wants to try the tool contradicts the "zero setup" promise.

Distribution is a single bundle built by esbuild. The reason is not the file size but the number of filesystem calls: every `import` in an unbundled `node_modules` is a separate resolve, and those are what make up the milliseconds measured below in ADR-003.
## Consequences
- Positive: `npx kadence` works straight away; event types are documentation and a check at the same time.
- Cost of the decision: 40 ms of the budget given to the runtime forever; the rest of the ADRs exist only because that price has already been paid.

- What will have to be reconsidered: if profiling shows that we consistently go past 200 ms even with an empty core, the only way out is to rewrite the core in Go and give up `npx` in favour of binaries. That decision is worth its own ADR and is not taken before measurements on real repositories exist.
